# Dependency & Reproducibility Checklist: Take the design-delta engine from the npm registry

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the engine-dependency change — do the spec, plan and tasks state reproducibility, sourcing and published-surface requirements completely, unambiguously and measurably?
**Created**: 2026-11-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the dependency's required source stated explicitly, rather than left to be inferred from what the lockfile happens to hold? [Completeness, Spec §Overview]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for the lockfile's state, separately from the `package.json` declaration? [Completeness, Spec §SC-2, §SC-5]
- [x] CHK003 Is the credential posture a copy-taker needs stated as a requirement, not only as a benefit? [Completeness, Spec §Scenario 4]
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec state what must happen if the published engine behaves differently from the build the gate previously read? [Completeness, Spec §SC-3]
- [x] CHK005 Are the published surfaces that must describe the dependency enumerated, rather than left as "the docs"? [Completeness, Plan §Surfaces touched]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the version range specified exactly, including its operator, rather than described as "pinned" or "current"? [Clarity, Spec §The range]
- [x] CHK007 Is the meaning of the caret on a `0.x` package spelled out, so a reviewer need not know npm's special case? [Clarity, Spec §The range]
- [x] CHK008 Is "the same findings at the same severities" anchored to a recorded artifact rather than to a remembered state? [Measurability, Spec §SC-3, Tasks §T001]
- [ ] CHK009 Can each success criterion be evaluated by running something, rather than by judgement? [Measurability, Spec §Success criteria]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do the spec, plan and tasks name the same dependency source and the same range form throughout? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK011 Does the Non-goals section agree with what the change actually does to the engine's content? [Consistency, Spec §Non-goals]
- [x] CHK012 Is the rejected alternative recorded with the reason it was rejected, so a later pass cannot re-adopt it by default? [Consistency, Spec §Why this]

## Scenario & Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK013 Are requirements stated for both install paths a copy-taker can take, `npm ci` and a lockfile-free `npm install`? [Coverage, Spec §Scenario 1, §Scenario 2]
- [x] CHK014 Is the case of a second, stale entry for the same dependency surviving elsewhere in the lockfile addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §SC-5]
- [x] CHK015 Is the case of the published version having moved since the spec was written addressed? [Edge Case, Tasks §T002]
- [x] CHK016 Are requirements stated for how a copy's owner deliberately moves to a later engine minor? [Coverage, Spec §Scenario 3, §SC-4]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK017 Is the claim that the package is published on the registry recorded with evidence a reviewer can re-check? [Assumption, Plan §Technical context]
- [x] CHK018 Is the assumption that no `.npmrc` is needed stated, with why it matters? [Assumption, Plan §Technical context]

## Reviewer pass — PM 2026-11-10

Answered against `spec.md` and `plan.md` at `20261109-144111-pin-engine-dependency`.
**17 of 18 satisfied; one left open, and it is not a `[Gap]` or a `[Conflict]`.**

- **CHK009 stays open.** Four of the five success criteria are runnable — two
  `node -e` reads, the gate plus a diff against a recorded baseline, and a
  `grep`. The fifth, SC-4, asks that `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md`
  describe how the engine arrives and how to move the range; that is judged by
  reading, not by running, and no phrasing makes a prose requirement
  executable. Recorded as an accepted limit of a documentation criterion
  rather than ticked, so the next reviewer sees the judgement instead of a
  tick that overstates it.
- **CHK011 was a real finding and is fixed, not waived.** Before this pass the
  Non-goals claimed the engine's version was not changing while the lockfile
  pinned a commit taken before `0.27.0` was published. Both `spec.md` and
  `plan.md` now say the content may move and name SC-3 as what gates it.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
